issue_context.title: API Proposal: C# 10 interpolated strings support, part 2
comments:
We didn't finish this in API Review, here were the notes so far

* InterpolatedBuilderArgumentAttribute: AllowMultiple should be false
* String.Format(IFormatProvider, InterpolatedStringBuilder) should take the builder as ref (because it's a mutable ref struct)

review_comments: I don't think I saw a test that hits this.  Either from a bad implementation reporting a negative number, or too big of one.
In `StringBuilder` you were defensive against bad TryFormat implementations reporting they wrote out of bounds, but here you weren't.
I did so in StringBuilder because it uses unsafe code that might trust the values in its length fields.  Here we just index into spans.

Thanks.

> we're starting to play a little fast and loose with type & memory safety

I guess I don't see how this has anything to do with type / memory safety.  Nothing promises that the destination buffer is zeroes. It might result in a gibberish string, but it's not breaking type safety, not causing the runtime to go off and do wacky things (and if it is, that's a bug in the runtime to be fixed), not causing the runtime to misinterpret one type for another, etc.  It's no more dangerous than writing random data into the destination span of a String.Create call, or calling `new string(randomCharArray)`.

Since AppendFormattedSlow is only called when _hasCustomFormatter was true (already returned), value was null (already returned) or TryCopyTo failed, we can be pretty certain the body of this if is unreachable, right?

I'd probably put a Debug.Fail in it to justify its uncovered state to someone looking at ccov.
Isn't this a behavior change? Interpolated strings use current culture, not invariant.
No,  these are all non-negative Int32s... culture doesn't influence the default formatting of such values.

I assume `format` is an ignored argument because

a) The pattern requires it.
b) `string.Format("{0:X}", "hi");` doesn't complain that format specifiers make no sense in context, so we won't here?
@stephentoub, just curious, has the default of string interpolation changed from current culture to InvariantCulture?
No.  But this is a non-negative integer.  Its default formatting is unaffected by culture.
